name: Annotate raw data
summary: Adds annotations to raw MEG/EEG data with MNE-Python from a table whose rows can be scoped by subject, session, task, run, tag or dataset, and outputs the annotated raw .fif.
description: Parses a delimited annotation table (onset, duration, description, optional channels and filter columns), applies the rows that match the input's identity, and sets them with raw.set_annotations, appending to or replacing existing annotations. Use it to apply one shared table of bad segments or events across many recordings. strict turns unmatched or out-of-range rows into errors.

outputs.description: Raw data with the annotations from the table added.

parameters.description: Annotation table, one annotation per row, with a header row. Required columns: onset (s from first sample), duration (s), description. Optional: channels (separated by ; or |), and filter columns subject, session, task, run, tag, dataset_id restricting the row to matching inputs (wildcards * ? [12], or re:<regex>). Rows without filters apply to every input. Delimiter: comma or tab.
parameters.placeholder: onset, duration, description[, channels, subject, session, task, run, tag, dataset_id]  (a header row naming the columns is required)

parameters.description: append keeps the annotations already in the file; replace discards them (only for inputs that at least one table row applies to).
Treat a row that matches no input, or lies outside the recording, as an error instead of a warning.

citations.text: Hayashi S, Caron BA, Heinsfeld AS, et al. brainlife.io: a decentralized and open-source cloud platform to support neuroscience research. Nat Methods 21:809-813 (2024).
Gramfort A, et al. MEG and EEG data analysis with MNE-Python. Front Neurosci 7:267 (2013).
